text:
Elias Pettersson the defenseman (not to be confused with the Canucks' center of the same name) is a 22-year-old from Vasteras, a third-round pick in 2022 who has worked his way into a regular role in Vancouver. He's playing 19 minutes a night, with 53 hits and 43 blocks.

The points have dried up: none in 12 straight games, on 2.5 expected, with his chances thinning out. He has three goals and four points in 25 games. The Canucks have scored 4.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, so some of that is luck.

The defensive numbers are the concern. Vancouver gets only 39% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, though the team isn't better without him. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season says he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league, which explains part of it, but opponents also got a lot more chances with him out there.

His minutes have swung wildly, from 12 to 26 in recent games. What to watch: whether the Canucks settle on a role for him.
